name: Claude
tagline: AI assistant for writing, reasoning, coding, and document work

pricing.notes: Official Anthropic pricing/support checked 2026-07-30; Pro listed at $20/month and $200/year.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: 200K context window; message allowance varies with demand and resets approximately every 5 hours.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: 200K context window; higher usage than Free.
tiers.notes: Annual plan is $200 paid upfront; the live page rounds the effective rate to $17/month.

tiers.name: Team Premium
tiers.limits: Minimum 2 members; about 5× Team Standard usage; 200K context window.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: 500K context window; included token allowance is 0 and model usage is billed separately at API rates.
tiers.notes: Annual-only seat price; usage charges are additional.

pricing.freeTierCaps: 200K context window; variable message allowance that resets approximately every 5 hours
pricing.billingTerms: Pro and Team offer monthly + annual; Max is monthly only; Enterprise is annual-only plus metered usage
pricing.hiddenCosts: Paid plans can enable extra-usage credits billed at API rates. Fable 5 usage on Pro and Team Standard has been pay-as-you-go from the first token since 2026-07-20.

verdictSummary: A Claude-like UI is trivial; the model, safety/reliability layer, long-context performance, artifacts/projects, and platform distribution are not.
coreLoopDIY: Build a chat app using Anthropic API, with document upload, conversation storage, and optional project contexts.
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay because the quality sits in the model and product platform, not the wrapper.

priorArt.name: LibreChat
priorArt.desc: Open-source multi-model AI chat platform for self-hosting API-based assistants.

alternatives.name: AnythingLLM
alternatives.desc: A private AI desk for documents and agents; install it, then choose local models or somebody else's meter.

facts.install: Native desktop installer, or Docker for a shared/self-hosted server
facts.engines: Local llama.cpp and imported GGUF models, plus Ollama, LM Studio, LocalAI and numerous cloud providers including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Azure, AWS Bedrock, Groq, Mistral, Cohere, and OpenRouter.
facts.dataFormat: Desktop data stays in the app's local data directory; the Docker edition persists its server storage volume, including an SQLite database and the default LanceDB vector store. Configured cloud providers receive the prompts and files sent to them.
facts.gapVsPaid: It does not include Anthropic inference, so matching Claude's reasoning and document quality requires a separately metered Anthropic API key or a usually weaker local model.
facts.setupBlocker: A non-expert must choose a model path: download a local model with enough RAM, connect Ollama or LM Studio correctly, or bring and pay for an API key.

alternatives.name: Big-AGI
alternatives.desc: A local-first multi-model workspace with files, search, code and personas; the interface assumes you enjoy buttons.

facts.install: Use the hosted web app, or deploy the Next.js app yourself
facts.engines: Connects to more than twenty backends, including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, OpenRouter, Azure OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, Groq, Mistral, DeepSeek, Ollama, LM Studio, LocalAI, and OpenAI-compatible endpoints.
facts.dataFormat: In the browser edition, provider keys and settings are stored in localStorage and chats, files, personas, and related workspace data in IndexedDB; configured model providers receive submitted content. There is no included cross-device cloud sync.
facts.gapVsPaid: Big-AGI offers a multi-model shell rather than Claude's included Anthropic models, first-party Projects and Artifacts workflow, and managed synchronization.
facts.setupBlocker: The first obstacle is bringing provider keys or a local endpoint; the app warns that browser-stored keys are plain text and protected only by the browser profile.

alternatives.name: Cherry Studio
alternatives.desc: A desktop model switchboard with assistants, files, agents and MCP; bring keys or make your laptop sweat.

facts.install: Native macOS, Windows, or Linux desktop installer
facts.engines: Supports hundreds of models through providers such as OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, OpenRouter, Azure, AWS Bedrock, Groq, DeepSeek, Mistral, Ollama, LM Studio, and other OpenAI-compatible services.
facts.dataFormat: Chats, API keys, assistants, settings, and local knowledge-base data are kept on the device; optional backup can use local files or WebDAV, while configured model providers receive prompts and attachments.
facts.gapVsPaid: It does not bundle Claude usage, and its desktop-first workspace is less seamless for Claude's first-party document, project, and cross-device workflow.
facts.setupBlocker: The installer is easy, but useful output requires either a paid provider key or downloading and running a local model that fits the machine.

alternatives.name: Jan
alternatives.desc: A local-first desktop assistant with cloud connectors and tools; your RAM gets the invoice.

facts.install: Native macOS, Windows, or Linux desktop installer
facts.engines: Runs local GGUF models through llama.cpp and Apple-silicon models through MLX, and connects to OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, Groq, Mistral, Azure, OpenRouter, Hugging Face, and custom OpenAI-compatible APIs.
facts.dataFormat: Models, assistants, files, and settings stay in Jan's data folder; threads are stored as local JSON and JSONL files. Cloud providers receive only the conversations or files routed to them.
facts.gapVsPaid: The free local route usually gives up Claude's reasoning and long-document quality, while connecting Anthropic turns the replacement back into metered API spend.
facts.setupBlocker: The first choice is consequential: local models need a sizable download and enough RAM, while cloud models require separately billed API keys.

alternatives.name: LibreChat
alternatives.desc: A self-hosted model switchboard with agents, files and tools; free software, paid model bills if you use paid models.

facts.engines: Connects to OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Vertex AI, Azure OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, Mistral, Groq, custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints, and local backends exposed through compatible APIs.
facts.dataFormat: The default stack stores conversations and accounts in MongoDB, search indexes in Meilisearch, and uploaded or RAG files in local volumes or configured object/vector storage; every configured model provider receives the requests routed to it.
facts.gapVsPaid: LibreChat can call Anthropic but does not include it, and it replaces Claude's managed service with a MongoDB-based system the user must secure and maintain.
facts.setupBlocker: It needs Docker, environment secrets, provider keys, storage, backups, and an admin; the official guide also documents a MongoDB image override because the default image crashes on Apple-silicon Macs.

alternatives.name: LM Studio
alternatives.desc: A local-model desktop lab with chat, documents and tools; free forever, but your hardware is now the cloud.

facts.install: Native desktop installer or Linux AppImage
facts.engines: Runs downloaded open-weight GGUF and safetensors models locally through llama.cpp and MLX-compatible runtimes, and exposes local OpenAI-compatible APIs.
facts.dataFormat: Downloaded models live in LM Studio's local model directory and chats are stored as local JSON conversation files; local inference does not send prompts to a model provider.
facts.gapVsPaid: Local open-weight models usually fall short of Claude's strongest reasoning, writing, and long-document performance, and LM Studio lacks Claude's managed project workflow.
facts.setupBlocker: The first obstacle is hardware: LM Studio recommends 16 GB RAM, requires current supported operating systems and CPU features, and useful models can occupy many gigabytes.

alternatives.name: Open WebUI
alternatives.desc: ChatGPT-shaped self-hosting with models, files, search and tools; the software is free, the admin role is yours.

facts.install: Docker is the recommended path; pip, uv, Kubernetes, and desktop-packaged paths are also documented
facts.engines: Connects natively to Ollama and OpenAI-compatible APIs, with documented support for providers and gateways such as OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Azure, Groq, Mistral, OpenRouter, and local inference servers.
facts.dataFormat: A default single-node install persists accounts and chats in webui.db (SQLite), embeddings in Chroma, and uploads in the Open WebUI data volume; larger deployments can move these to PostgreSQL, Redis, and external vector or object stores.
facts.gapVsPaid: It can front Anthropic-compatible access but supplies neither Claude usage nor Anthropic's first-party Projects and Artifacts experience, while adding server administration.
facts.setupBlocker: The first obstacle is owning the service: Docker volumes, a model backend or API key, user security, updates, and backups; an unpersisted container loses the data.

alternatives.name: LobeHub
alternatives.desc: A polished agents-and-files workspace; self-hosting is free and frontier inference usually is not.

facts.install: Hosted signup, one-click Vercel deployment, or Docker Compose for the server-database edition
facts.engines: Supports more than seventy providers and gateways, including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, Azure OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, OpenRouter, Groq, DeepSeek, Ollama, LM Studio, and OpenAI-compatible endpoints.
facts.dataFormat: Local mode keeps chats in browser IndexedDB and supports JSON export; server mode uses PostgreSQL for account and conversation data plus S3-compatible object storage for files. Configured providers receive routed prompts and attachments.
facts.gapVsPaid: Using Claude through LobeHub still requires separately billed Anthropic access, and self-hosted server mode is materially more complex than Claude's managed workspace.
facts.setupBlocker: Hosted use still requires model credentials or purchased inference, while serious self-hosting adds PostgreSQL, object storage, authentication, secrets, a domain, and migration from browser-local data.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Msty
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The desktop core is $0, but the terms limit it to private non-commercial use; paid work needs a license.

notes: Good no that still points technical readers to usable wrappers.
prompt:
Build me a personal chat client on the Anthropic API to replace my Claude Pro
subscription with per-token billing. Requirements:

- A local web app: Node + Express + better-sqlite3, streaming replies over SSE,
  a conversation sidebar, Markdown rendering with marked.
- Anthropic API key in .env; model picker with Sonnet as the default and Opus
  on demand; system prompt editable and saved per project.
- Projects: a project groups conversations and holds a few reference docs
  (plain text or PDF via pdf-parse) prepended as context for every chat inside
  it.
- Use prompt caching on the project docs to cut token costs, the API supports
  it directly.
- SQLite FTS5 search across all conversations; export any thread to Markdown.
- A cost meter per conversation plus a monthly total from the API usage fields,
  so the keep-paying-or-not decision is a number, not a feeling.
- Localhost only, no accounts, no telemetry.
- Out of scope: artifacts, mobile apps, and agent features. If the cost meter
  shows heavy use, flat-rate Pro or Max wins; include that comparison logic in
  the README.
- README: key setup, a link to current per-token prices, and state that the
  model is the product; this wrapper only changes how I pay for it.
